proposals.subject: Document-based reporting resource: Trafigura funding and margin liquidity
proposals.body:
Hello GTR editorial team,

l0g has published an English investigation into the banks and facilities behind Trafigura's oil trading. It follows public facility announcements, accounts and financial-stability documents to distinguish committed lending, drawn debt, collateral and the cash required for margin calls.

The reporting resource is here: https://l0g.fr/en/analysis/banking-on-oil-2-banks-financing-trafigura/

It does not infer individual bank exposures from a lender list. Sources and limits are attached to the analysis. If useful for your reporting, l0g's original text and figures can be reused under CC BY 4.0 with attribution, a link to this investigation and an indication of changes; third-party material retains its own rights.

Citation guidance and primary-document links: https://l0g.fr/en/press-resources/#investigations

Olivier Laurelli / l0g.fr

proposals.subject: Reporting resource: Cortina, follow-form capital and underwriting incentives
proposals.body:
Hello Reinsurance News editorial team,

l0g has published an English analysis of the proposed Cortina structure and the underwriting questions around additional follow-form capital. The piece examines risk selection, pricing incentives, portfolio concentration and the right to decline business.

Analysis: https://l0g.fr/en/analysis/aon-blackstone-cortina-reinsurance-risk-pricing/

It distinguishes reported proposals from final approvals. Its numerical examples explain the mechanism and are not forecasts of Cortina losses or savings. Lloyd's guidance and the FCA broker-market study are linked alongside the reporting.

If useful for a follow-up, l0g's original text and figures are reusable under CC BY 4.0 with attribution, a direct link and an indication of changes. Third-party sources retain their own rights. Citation guidance: https://l0g.fr/en/press-resources/#investigations

Olivier Laurelli / l0g.fr

proposals.subject: Story idea: insurance coverage and the future receivables behind Greensill
proposals.body:
Hello Insurance Journal editorial team,

A potential educational angle for agents and brokers: how an insurance policy interacts with the receivable being financed, its maturity and a fund's redemption terms. l0g's English Greensill investigation follows parliamentary documents, FINMA findings and the public record of subsequent investor and insurance disputes.

Analysis: https://l0g.fr/en/analysis/greensill-insurance-future-receivables-risk/

Suggested outline: identifying the underlying obligation; separating insurance cover from permission to finance further business; following the withdrawal and redemption timetable. The piece retains uncertainty around disputed coverage and confidential settlement terms.

l0g's original text and figures are reusable under CC BY 4.0 with attribution, a direct link and an indication of changes. Third-party material retains its own rights. Citation guidance: https://l0g.fr/en/press-resources/#investigations

Olivier Laurelli / l0g.fr
